In both versions duckdb_query returned success and the canary bytes were completely untouched (write stayed within exactly the first 48 bytes). So all three checkpoints spanning the full pinned range (1.3.2 via header diff, 1.4.0 and 1.5.1 via live ABI probe) confirm 48 bytes is exact, not merely coincidentally unchanged. Given DuckDB's own no-ABI-break policy for the C API plus the by-design opaque-pointer indirection, there is no plausible in-range release that enlarges this struct; the scenario is not just unconfirmed but actively contradicted by the mechanism DuckDB uses to avoid exactly this. The recommendation (derive size from the loaded library or assert at import) is reasonable generic defensive hygiene but is not addressing an actual or credible memory-safety defect in the current or realistically-reachable tree, so it does not stand as a MEM finding at any severity.

refuted.title: No duckdb version guard although hard-coded pybind11/ABI offsets are validated only on 1.3.2 while the pin allows <1.6
refuted.description: extract_connection_ptr hard-codes two ABI offsets: id(conn)+16 (line 59) to read the DuckDBPyConnection C++ object pointer and cpp_obj_p+32 (line 62) to read the unique_ptr<Connection>. The docstring (lines 31-34) states these are 'Validated on duckdb 1.3.2 / Linux x86-64 / libstdc++' and that the layout 'may change with major duckdb releases'. However the project pin is duckdb>=1.3.2,<1.6 (CLAUDE.md / pyproject), so 1.4.x and 1.5.x are permitted at runtime, and grep confirms there is no runtime version check anywhere in pybridge.py (no reference to duckdb.__version__, duckdb_library_version, etc.). If any in-range release changes the pybind11 holder layout or the DuckDBPyConnection field order, cpp_obj_p+32 reads a wrong word. The sibling contract this bridge is modeled on, numbox pysqlite_bridge.extract_connection_ptr, explicitly refuses to hand out the pointer when the underlying library is not coordinated (libraries_coordinated() check, pysqlite_bridge.py:159-161); numbduck has no analogous gate.
refuted.impact: On a permitted-but-unvalidated duckdb (1.4.x/1.5.x) or a non-libstdc++/non-x86-64 build, the offsets can silently resolve to a wrong pointer. Best case the SELECT 1 validation returns DuckDBError and a clean RuntimeError is raised; worst case duckdb_query(conn_ptr, ...) dereferences garbage and segfaults the interpreter before any rc can be inspected. Silent-wrong-pointer / crash risk that the current 'validated before returned' wording understates.
refuted.recommendation: Add a runtime guard that the offsets are only trusted on a known-good duckdb version/platform, e.g. check duckdb.__version__ against the validated set (or at minimum against the <1.6 pin ceiling) and raise a clear RuntimeError instructing the user to re-verify offsets when it does not match, mirroring numbox's libraries_coordinated() refuse-to-proceed pattern.
refuted.verdictReasoning: The code fact is real -- pybridge.py has no runtime duckdb version/platform check (grep of the file confirms no reference to duckdb.__version__ or any guard) and hardcodes id(conn)+16 (pybridge.py:59) then cpp_obj_p+32 (pybridge.py:62), while the pin (pyproject.toml duckdb>=1.3.2,<1.6) permits 1.4.x/1.5.x. But the finding's specific risk claim -- that an in-range release such as 1.4.x/1.5.x could silently change the layout so 'cpp_obj_p+32 reads a wrong word' -- is directly contradicted by conclusive evidence gathered two ways. (1) CI: .github/workflows/numbduck_ci.yml:24 runs the full pytest suite (no addopts/conftest filtering, confirmed no conftest.py exists) across duckdb-version matrix [1.3.2, 1.4.0, 1.5.1] on ubuntu-latest, ubuntu-24.04-arm, and windows-latest; this exercises all three call sites of extract_connection_ptr in test/test_ducklib.py (lines 2569, 2626, 2724, including the SELECT-1-validated path). The latest main run (28539203573, merge of PR #49, 2026-07-01) is GREEN 51/51 jobs, i.e. every matrix cell -- covering 1.4.0 and 1.5.1 on three OS/arch combos -- passed. (2) Direct reproduction performed here: installed duckdb 1.3.2, 1.4.0, and 1.5.1 into isolated pip --target dirs on this Linux x86-64 host and called numbduck.pybridge.extract_connection_ptr(conn) directly against each. All three returned a valid, C-API-validated Connection* (the function's own internal 'SELECT 1' check passed) with no error: 1.3.2 -> 0x3d17d730, 1.4.0 -> 0x1c610070, 1.5.1 -> 0x2e2c6740. This empirically confirms the id(conn)+16 / cpp_obj_p+32 offsets are stable across the entire currently-pinned-and-tested duckdb range on Linux x86-64, not merely 1.3.2 as the docstring conservatively claims. The numbox sibling-contract analogy (pysqlite_bridge.libraries_coordinated()) is also an imperfect match: that gate detects two divergent *already-loaded* libsqlite3 copies (the macOS dyld-shared-cache scenario), a materially different failure mode from single-library cross-release ABI drift, so it doesn't establish that an equivalent guard is straightforwardly applicable here. Given the claimed 'high' severity rests entirely on speculative breakage for 1.4.x/1.5.x that has now been shown not to occur (both via exhaustive CI and independent direct reproduction), the finding as characterized is refuted. What legitimately remains is a much narrower, lower-value hardening point: (a) no macOS runner exists in the CI matrix at all (arch: ubuntu-latest/ubuntu-24.04-arm/windows-latest only), so the docstring's 'Linux x86-64/libstdc++' scope is honest and macOS is genuinely untested -- but that is a platform-coverage gap, not the duckdb-version-drift risk the finding names; and (b) a defense-in-depth version/platform assertion is still reasonable to add proactively for versions released after this review. Neither rises to 'high severity active bug'; at most a 'low' severity, nice-to-have hardening recommendation.

refuted.title: Allocators hand out a bare ndarray whose .ctypes.data is a dangling-pointer footgun if the array is not bound to a live name
refuted.description: Every allocator returns a plain owned numpy.int64 array (allocate_buffer at duckdb_utils.py:8, via create_duckdb_* at lines 13/19/25/31/37/43/49). The buffer's lifetime is entirely caller-managed and there is no coupling between the buffer object and the handle/struct DuckDB writes into it. The whole out-param protocol depends on the caller keeping the *array* alive (not just the extracted handle int) for as long as DuckDB needs that memory: for single-handle buffers, until the matching duckdb_destroy_*(buf.ctypes.data); for the 48-byte duckdb_result buffer (create_duckdb_result, line 37), until duckdb_destroy_result reads internal_data out of the live struct. Because the allocator yields a bare ndarray, the idiomatic numpy footgun `p = create_duckdb_result().ctypes.data` (take .ctypes.data of an unbound temporary) leaves `p` dangling the instant the temporary is collected, and DuckDB's subsequent execute/destroy writes/reads freed heap. This is a real property of the API and is unchanged by the @proxy migration (duckdb_utils.py was not touched). It is not currently triggered — every caller binds the array to a named local first (e.g. pybridge.py:65 'result', online_scoring.py:153 'stmt' kept alive across the JIT loop; test_ducklib.py create_* uses). So this is a latent hazard the buffer API invites, not a present defect.
refuted.impact: If any future caller (or example/doc copied by a user) writes the natural-looking `create_duckdb_result().ctypes.data` / `create_duckdb_*().ctypes.data` one-liner, the array is GC'd immediately and DuckDB writes the result struct (or a handle) into freed memory — heap corruption / use-after-free, silent and intermittent. The 48-byte result buffer is the highest-stakes case because DuckDB stores the whole struct there and destroy dereferences it.
refuted.recommendation: Document on the allocators (duckdb_utils.py:7-51) that the returned array must outlive all DuckDB use of its .ctypes.data — the buffer, not the extracted handle int, is what must stay alive — or have callers/helpers take the buffer and its pointer in two explicit steps. No code change is strictly required since no caller is currently affected; treat as an API-safety note.
refuted.verdictReasoning: Read current numbduck/duckdb_utils.py in full: allocate_buffer (line 8) and every create_duckdb_* (lines 13/19/25/31/37/43/49) match the candidate's description exactly — @njit allocators returning a bare numpy.int64 ndarray with no lifetime coupling to the DuckDB handle/struct written into it. The general hazard described (an unbound `create_duckdb_result().ctypes.data` one-liner dangles once the temporary array is refcount-collected) is a real, technically accurate property of numpy/NRT-backed arrays and is unchanged by the @proxy migration, so this does not fail on 'not real' grounds in isolation. However, it fails both refutation tests taken together: (1) the CURRENT review's own findings/DBU-MEM.json 'notes' field already directly analyzes this exact hazard — 'The ".ctypes.data does not keep the array alive" hazard (p = create_duckdb_result().ctypes.data) is a CALLER responsibility, and every in-repo caller binds the array to a local first (pybridge.py:65 "result", online_scoring.py:153 "stmt", all create_* uses in test_ducklib.py), so no use-after-free is actually present in the tree' — language the reconcile mapper's own justification quotes near-verbatim. This shows the current reviewers examined this precise hazard with full knowledge of the codebase and deliberately declined to promote it to a formal finding, judging it a documented non-issue (latent, hypothetical-future-caller-only, no live defect) rather than an oversight. (2) Checked docs/reviews/2026-07-01-numbduck/reconcile/new-index.json: no formal finding ID is dedicated to this ctypes.data-lifetime hazard, but its substance is already fully captured as an explicit, reasoned exclusion in the current review's own artifacts (DBU-MEM.json notes), which sit alongside the current DBU-MEM-1 finding (a different, more concrete memory-safety issue at the same file/line: hard-coded 48-byte result buffer vs duckdb 1.3.2-1.6 struct-size drift). Adding REC-DBU-MEM-1 as a new formal 'low/low' finding would duplicate analysis the review pipeline already performed and consciously chose not to elevate, rather than surface a defect the review missed. Given the default-REFUTED stance and the requirement for conclusive evidence to adopt, this does not clear the bar: refuted.

refuted.title: Two scalar-function wrappers (get_extra_info / set_error) stranded at EOF, separated from the scalar block
refuted.description: duckdb_scalar_function_get_extra_info (wrapper at ducklib.py:1399, sig key at 272) and duckdb_scalar_function_set_error (wrapper at 1405, sig key at 273) sit appended at the very end of the file, after the aggregate-function wrapper block (ends 1396) and immediately before the four struct-by-value bind wrappers (1411+). Every other scalar-function wrapper is grouped in the scalar block at 1213-1312, and every other scalar sig key is in the scalar sig block at 239-255. These two are the residue of a later append. (The four orphaned bind wrappers that share this EOF cluster are already reported by current findings DCK-sig-DES-1 and DCK-wrap-DES-2; this covers only the two scalar wrappers those findings omit.)
refuted.impact: A maintainer scanning the scalar-function wrapper run (1213-1312) sees the block as complete and may re-add a duplicate get_extra_info/set_error wrapper, or edit one copy. The grouping invariant erodes silently; 'is this scalar function bound?' scans and diff review become unreliable. No runtime effect — all @proxy decorators look up by name and the signatures dict is complete.
refuted.recommendation: Relocate the two scalar wrappers into the scalar block (1213-1312) and move sig keys 272-273 up into the scalar sig block (239-255), alongside the bind-wrapper relocation already recommended.
refuted.verdictReasoning: DUPLICATE. The current-tree defect is real (verified: get_extra_info wrapper at ducklib.py:1399-1402, set_error at 1405-1408, both after the aggregate block ending 1396 and before the bind wrappers at 1411+; sig keys at 272-273 after the aggregate sig block, separated from the scalar sig block ending ~255) — but it is already fully reported by the CURRENT finding DCK-sig-DES-1 (docs/reviews/2026-07-01-numbduck/findings/DCK-sig-DES.json), not just the four bind wrappers as the reconcile mapper's justification claims. DCK-sig-DES-1's full description text explicitly states: 'The same split affects duckdb_scalar_function_get_extra_info/duckdb_scalar_function_set_error, whose sig entries (272-273) and wrappers (1399-1408) are separated from the rest of the scalar-function group (sigs 239-255, wrappers 1213-1312) by the entire aggregate block.' Its recommendation likewise explicitly says to 'move duckdb_scalar_function_get_extra_info/set_error into the scalar-function wrapper group' alongside the bind-wrapper relocation. The mapper in reconcile/DCK-sig-DES.json apparently compared only against the short gist summaries in reconcile/new-index.json (which truncate to ~200 chars and omit this sentence) rather than the full finding body in findings/DCK-sig-DES.json, and concluded the scalar wrappers were unmentioned when in fact they are named explicitly, with matching line numbers (1399-1408, sig keys 272-273). No new finding should be adopted; DCK-sig-DES-1 already covers this exact defect in full.

refuted.title: Validation RuntimeError lacks diagnostic context (no duckdb version, offsets, or layout-drift hint)
refuted.description: When the round-trip SELECT 1 validation fails, the helper raises RuntimeError('extracted connection pointer failed validation') (pybridge.py:70-72) with no context: it does not report the running duckdb.__version__ (duckdb is already imported at line 3), the offsets used (+16 at line 59, +32 at line 62), or the most likely root cause on an in-pin-range (>=1.3.2,<1.6) 1.4/1.5 wheel — an unvalidated/drifted pybind11/DuckDBPyConnection layout. The function's own docstring (lines 31-34) identifies version-dependent layout as the primary failure mode, so this error is the natural place to surface that hypothesis.
refuted.impact: A user hitting this on a newer, permitted-but-unvalidated duckdb gets a generic message and no pointer toward the actual root cause (offset/layout drift), slowing diagnosis of precisely the fragility this code is most exposed to.
refuted.recommendation: Include duckdb.__version__ and a hint to re-verify the pybind11/DuckDBPyConnection offsets in the RuntimeError message (e.g. note the validated version 1.3.2 and that the layout may have changed for the running version).
refuted.verdictReasoning: Refuted as DUPLICATE. The cited code is verbatim on the current tree (numbduck/pybridge.py:69-72: `if rc != ducklib.DuckDBSuccess: raise RuntimeError("extracted connection pointer failed validation")`), so the NOT-REAL path fails -- the message really is context-free. But the underlying defect (no diagnostic pointer toward duckdb-version/offset drift as the likely root cause of a validation failure) is already covered in substance by the current PBR unit's own findings on this exact site: PBR-COR-1 (high) and PBR-DES-2 (medium) both target lines 59/62/28-34 and recommend adding a duckdb.__version__ guard that 'raise[s] a clear RuntimeError instructing the user to re-verify offsets' / 'names the offsets to re-verify when an untested version is detected' -- i.e. exactly the diagnostic content (version + offsets + re-verify hint) the candidate wants surfaced. Critically, PBR-DES-1 (medium, same file lines 28-72) already analyzes this precise RuntimeError branch and concludes it is 'effectively dead' for the version-drift scenario: a wrong-offset conn_ptr causes duckdb_query to dereference a wild pointer (UB/segfault) BEFORE any rc is produced, so this rc!=DuckDBSuccess branch in practice only fires for a live-but-erroring connection, not for the layout-drift case the candidate assumes is diagnosed here. PBR-DES-1's recommendation is to reword the docstring and pair it with PBR-COR-1's version guard -- which is the correct fix locus for the version/offset-drift diagnostic, not the reactive message at line 70-72. The candidate's premise ('this error is the natural place to surface that hypothesis') is the exact overstatement PBR-DES-1 already flags. The reconciler's distinction ('different, not-yet-existing code path') is not a meaningful basis to adopt a second low-severity finding for the same underlying gap already addressed by PBR-COR-1 + PBR-DES-1 + PBR-DES-2 in combination. No corrected severity needed since the finding is not adopted.

refuted.title: Windows sret/by-pointer struct ABI and macOS library-download branches are unexercised
refuted.description: All struct-by-value tests (hugeint 835, uhugeint 853, interval 871, decimal 891, and the create/get value equivalents 1263-1327) plus every UDF/UDAF path run only on SysV x86-64 (Linux/WSL2, confirmed by the benchmark docstring at 2693). The Windows branches of _call_lib_func_struct_in/out (arg-by-pointer / sret return) and the macOS library-acquisition/download path in the loader are never hit by this suite; there is no xfail/skip marker documenting them as platform-conditional either. Given the pin duckdb>=1.3.2,<1.6 and cross-platform intent, these ABI/loader branches ship untested.
refuted.impact: A Windows-only ABI regression (struct passed/returned via the wrong convention) or a macOS-only loader/download failure would not be caught by CI, which is Linux-only.
refuted.recommendation: Either add a Windows CI leg that runs the struct-by-value tests, or add explicit skip markers with reason so the platform gap is visible; add a targeted loader test for the macOS/download branch (can be mocked).
refuted.verdictReasoning: The finding is a compound claim (Windows struct-ABI branches unexercised + macOS loader/download branches unexercised) and its central, severity-driving half is factually wrong on the current tree. First, on naming: the functions the finding cites, `_call_lib_func_struct_in` / `_call_lib_func_struct_out`, do not exist anywhere in the current codebase. Verified via grep across /home/erik/projects/numbduck/numbduck/ducklib.py (1432 lines total) -- no `struct_in`, `struct_out`, `_is_win`-gated branch, `@intrinsic`, or `optnone` usage remains; every struct-by-value binding (duckdb_bind_hugeint/uhugeint/interval/decimal at ducklib.py:1411-1432, duckdb_create/get_varint at 726-729/1051-1054) now calls the generic `_call_lib_func` intrinsic imported from numbox.core.bindings.call, exactly per the task's CURRENT-TREE FACTS. This confirms the CLAUDE.md 'Struct-by-value helpers' section and its 'Follow-ups' migration note (which cites ducklib.py:1525-1640, past the file's actual 1432-line end) are stale documentation describing an earlier architecture; the migration to `_call_lib_func` has already happened for hugeint/uhugeint/interval/decimal/varint alike. Second, and decisively: the finding's impact claim -- 'would not be caught by CI, which is Linux-only' -- is false. Read /home/erik/projects/numbduck/.github/workflows/numbduck_ci.yml: the `arch` matrix explicitly includes `windows-latest` (with python 3.11 + duckdb 1.5.1, both numba 0.60.0 and 0.64.0 legs after the Windows-narrowing excludes), `runs-on: "${{ matrix.arch }}"`, and the 'Test with pytest' step runs a bare `pytest` with no platform filter. There is no conftest.py, no module-level `sys.platform`/`win32` skip, and no per-test skip marker in test/test_ducklib.py (grepped for `platform`, `win32`, `darwin`, `skipif` -- only two unrelated version-gated `skipif`s at lines 1341 and 2372). So the full struct-by-value suite -- test_bind_hugeint (835), test_bind_uhugeint (853), test_bind_interval (871), test_bind_decimal (891), and the create/get-value equivalents -- genuinely executes on windows-latest in CI, driving numbox's `_call_lib_func` (numbox/core/bindings/call.py:21-200) through its real Windows x64 branches: `_PLATFORM_WIN_X64` register-passable-size dispatch (lines 103-111, 150-158), `sret` for non-register-passable small/large structs (137-142, 183-193), and the byval/alloca-pointer path (166-171). The Windows ABI code path is therefore hit by CI, contrary to the finding's core claim. Only the second half of the compound finding survives: /home/erik/projects/numbduck/numbduck/utils.py's macOS-only `_download_libduckdb`/`_find_standalone_libduckdb`/`_MACOS_LIBDUCKDB_SEARCH_PATHS` (lines ~22-84) are genuinely never referenced by any test (grepped test/test_ducklib.py and test/test_init.py -- no hits), and numbduck_ci.yml has no macOS/darwin leg at all. That sub-claim alone would support a narrow, low-severity finding, but it is not what TST-cover-10 as written and titled asserts as its primary defect, and it does not rescue the finding's false 'CI is Linux-only' / Windows-untested characterization. Given the finding conflates a real gap (macOS loader) with a demonstrably false one (Windows ABI, backed by a nonexistent function-name citation), and the false half is what the title foregrounds and the impact statement is built on, the finding as stated is refuted.
